questions.question: What is the cell described as in the article?
options: The basic structural and functional unit of all forms of life
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all forms of life or organisms.'
Incorrect. The article does not describe cells as the smallest unit of matter.
Incorrect. The article describes cells as the basic unit of life, not as an organelle.
Incorrect. The article does not describe cells as a group of tissues.

questions.question: From which language does the term 'cell' come, and what does it mean?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says: 'The term comes from the Latin word cellula meaning 'small room'.'
Incorrect. The article specifies Latin, not Greek.
Incorrect. The article specifies Latin, not French.
Incorrect. The article specifies Latin, not German.

questions.question: What does a biological cell basically consist of?
options: A semipermeable cell membrane enclosing cytoplasm that contains genetic material
A rigid cell wall and a nucleus
Only a nucleus and a cell membrane
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'A biological cell basically consists of a semipermeable cell membrane enclosing cytoplasm that contains genetic material.'
Incorrect. The article does not mention a rigid cell wall in this description.
Incorrect. The article also includes cytoplasm and genetic material.
Incorrect. The article mentions a cell membrane, not a cell wall.

questions.question: Under what condition are most cells visible?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says: 'Most cells are only visible under a microscope.'
Incorrect. The article states that most cells are not visible with the naked eye.
Incorrect. The article specifies a microscope, not a magnifying glass.
Incorrect. The article specifies a microscope, not sunlight.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a highly-differentiated cell type mentioned in the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article mentions 'red blood cells' as an example of highly-differentiated cell types.
Incorrect. Skin cells are not mentioned as an example in the article.
Incorrect. Muscle cells are not mentioned as an example in the article.
Incorrect. Nerve cells are not mentioned as an example in the article.

questions.question: What are most cells capable of, except for highly-differentiated types?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'most cells are capable of replication, and protein synthesis.'
Incorrect. Photosynthesis is not mentioned as a general capability of most cells.
Incorrect. Movement and digestion are not mentioned as general capabilities.
Incorrect. Growth and division are not the exact capabilities listed.

questions.question: When did cells emerge on Earth according to the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says: 'Cells emerged on Earth about four billion years ago.'
Incorrect. The article states four billion years, not two.
Incorrect. The article states four billion years, not one.
Incorrect. The article states four billion years, not six.

questions.question: What are the two groups into which all organisms are classified?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'All organisms are grouped into prokaryotes and eukaryotes.'
Incorrect. Plants and animals are not the main groups mentioned.
Incorrect. Single-celled and multicellular are descriptions, not the main groups.
Incorrect. Bacteria and archaea are subgroups of prokaryotes, not the main groups.

questions.question: Which of the following are described as single-celled prokaryotes?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says: 'Prokaryotes are single-celled and include archaea and bacteria.'
Incorrect. Protists and fungi are not described as prokaryotes.
Incorrect. Animals and plants are multicellular eukaryotes.
Incorrect. Algae and yeasts are not described as prokaryotes.

questions.question: Which of the following can be single-celled eukaryotes according to the article?
options: Most protists, some fungi, and some algae
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'Single-celled eukaryotes include most protists, some species of fungi (yeasts), and some species of algae.'
Incorrect. Animals and plants are multicellular, not single-celled.
Incorrect. Bacteria are prokaryotes, not eukaryotes.
Incorrect. Archaea are prokaryotes, not eukaryotes.
